findings.F1: Inside the choppy-calm profile, the 5-day move after an up day is not graded the way the forecast assumes. On the 5-day grid, the excess return is -0.88 % after rises of 0 to 0.5 swing units (n 43), -2.67 % after 0.5 to 1 unit (n 24, t -1.64), +8.72 % after 1 to 1.5 units (n 11) and +3.72 % above 1.5 units (n 11, t 1.98). Rises above one 30-day swing earn +6.22 % in excess (total +6.92 %, n 22, t 2.17, strength 0.50). Rises below one swing lose. This is why the idea's size per case is -0.43 % (t -1.15, 651 cases) and its total move, +0.19 %, only equals the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: The book trades mostly the losing small rises. The forecast is each component standardised over its past 60 values and clipped at 0, so any ordinary up day gets a position. The median entry day was a rise of only 0.76 swing units, and just 32 % of the 98 entries rose more than one swing. On the grid, the bottom half of positive forecasts loses -1.80 % in excess over 5 days (n 48, t -1.50) and -5.36 % over 10 days. The top half gains +2.80 % (t 1.61) and +5.18 % over 10 days (t 1.92). The book's position-day mean is therefore 0.030 % a day against the 0.05 % required, and its Sharpe is 0.40 below holding.
findings.F3: Closeness to the 20-day high works as a multiplier of a large rise, not as a separate effect. In choppy markets, a rise above one swing that closes within 1 % of the 20-day closing high earns +14.97 % in excess over 5 days (n 8, t 2.39, strength 1.21). The same large rise further below the high earns +2.78 % (n 10, t 1.16). Being at the high with a rise of at most one swing earns -0.14 % (n 14, t -0.06), so the closeness condition alone is not an effect. Inside the profile, large rises at the high give +10.39 % (n 11, t 2.04). The equal-weight mean of the two components lets a near-high small rise trade on its own.
findings.F4: The book's falls come from these frequent weak trades, not from one bad window. The deepest fall of the chained daily book is -15.2 %, with its trough in w10. Falls of -14.0 % in w14, -14.4 % in w15 and -12.1 % in w9 show the same bleed spread across windows. Against a yearly return of +1.3 %, this gives a Calmar of 0.04. Large in-profile rises paid on every coin: their mean 5-day excess was +3.4 % to +19.1 % on all six coins (BTC +5.7 % n 4, XMR +3.4 % n 5, XRP +19.1 % n 3). XMR's trades still lost -1.46 % net on average, so its losses come from the small-rise entries.
findings.F5: The calm restriction holds. Outside the profile, rises above one swing earn +2.05 % in excess over 5 days (n 123, t 1.72), and +3.56 % at the 20-day high (n 60, t 1.88). That is about a third of the in-profile +6.22 % and +10.39 %. In falling markets, rises above 1.5 swings earn -0.10 % (n 11). In rising markets, rises above 1.5 swings earn +8.28 % (n 29, t 2.13), but rises of 1 to 1.5 swings earn -1.10 % there, so the grading is weaker outside choppy calm.
findings.F6: The effect of large rises still shows over 10 days inside the profile but fades in strength. Rises above one swing earn +7.02 % in excess over 10 days (n 11, t 1.60) against +6.22 % over 5 days. At the 20-day high, the excess over 20 days is +12.99 % (n 4). The 5-day horizon is right in order of size, and holding to 10 days keeps most of the move with half the trades.

ideas.idea: In a choppy, calm market, the further a coin's one-day rise exceeds the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the further it keeps rising over the next 5 days. Rises within the coin's usual daily swing carry no follow-through; the move grows with how many usual swings the day covered.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys only calm-market up days that are large against the coin's own swing and sizes up with the excess, refusing the ordinary up days that made this book lose.
ideas.name: calm outsized rise continues

ideas.idea: In a choppy, calm market, the larger a coin's one-day rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, when that rise closes the coin at its highest close of the past 20 days, the further it keeps rising over the next 5 days. A rise of the same size that ends well below the 20-day high continues much less.
ideas.consequence: A trader sizes a calm-market breakout by the day's rise in swing units times its closeness to the 20-day high, so a near-high day with a small rise, or a large bounce far below the high, gets little or nothing.
ideas.name: calm large breakout continues

ideas.idea: In a choppy, calm market, the larger a coin's one-day rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, and the closer that rise takes its close to its highest close of the past 20 days, the further it keeps rising over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader holds calm-market large up days near their highs for ten days rather than five, keeping the move while paying for half as many trades.
ideas.name: calm big rise, longer hold
